Store atmosphere & tips & overall review

Even when I passed by a few times in the winter,

reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
I looked it up on YouTube and looked it up on Manpple, and found that Miari Hotteok wasn't even registered here, so I registered it and stopped by on my way to Hapjeong.

The store was on the main street, so I parked in the alley for a while and went inside the store to find only one customer who had probably ordered several take-out items.

I saw on YouTube that you have to make a reservation in advance to purchase it, so I called in advance and he said it was okay since he wasn't busy right now.

Sunlight pours in from all directions in the bright, small shop, and the owner is hard at work making hotteok (hotteok), while his wife is hard at work grilling hotteok (hotteok) on a special hotteok grill.

When I told her that I was only going to eat one since I was the one who called earlier, the wife asked for my understanding to bake only one first for the customer who had ordered several take-out items and started grilling mine.

While my wife was baking one of my hotteoks, she was exchanging stories with customers who came to order take-out, saying that the hotteoks here are popular and that they are delicious even when frozen and taken out. I also feel good when I see customers talking with pride about visiting from many countries.

He put the flat hotteok dough on a clean hotteok grilling pan without oil, covered it with a lid with a handle, waited a bit, opened it, flipped the hotteok over three times, and asked me to take a picture now. When I took the picture, he placed the hotteok on the table and demonstrated how to eat it.

He told us to tear the hotteok flour bread with our hands and to tear it little by little and dip it into the brown sugar filling inside.

When I tasted it, it felt like a large ball bread with brown sugar filling on the inside, which I don't know if it was baked in oil, but it wasn't crispy like ball bread, but it was a soft and chewy wheat bread, with a slight smell of flour, and the taste of the brown sugar inside was sweet. It lacked the cinnamon flavor and was sweeter than I wanted, but it was still delicious.

It was especially good because it wasn't grilled in oil, which I sometimes miss when it's fried with brown sugar filling.

I ate it all in no time and left the store, saying I would stop by again.

Overall, it's a store that serves a hotteok version of my favorite gonggalbbang. I want to visit again because I like the light and sweet brown sugar filling that isn't baked in oil. They say it's delicious even when frozen from the freezer, so next time I bought several and ordered them to take out and tried freezing them in the freezer.

reviews.author: My Gumi
reviews.text:
After going to another famous ramen restaurant, I threw away my money and, with an open mind, decided that cheap ramen would suit my taste and went to any ramen restaurant attached to a department store.

Why do people always hit the jackpot where they least expect it?

Jiro Ramen is a legendary ramen restaurant with its main branch in Hongdae and the only branch here.

Naturally, Japanese ramen is salty.

If you go to the mainland and order ramen, it's really spicy, but of course?

It's too greasy for our tastes.

There are many options to choose from when ordering through the tablet kiosks placed at each table.

It was possible to choose the degree of doneness of the noodles and the thickness of the broth.

If it were me, I would have noticed right away, but at that time, I was throwing away money in various places and just moved on, as if the feeling of anticipation was a luxury.

Is this set number 2? If you do this, you can get rice and ramen as a set.

Among other stores, some that are a bit more clumsy do not allow you to change the ramen in the set, but here you can change to any ramen.

As for the taste of the rice, at first it had a texture and aroma as if egg yolk had been secretly added to the soy sauce. Hmm?? I thought there was no yolk in it and kept eating it.

Even though it seemed like the soy sauce was sprinkled roughly on top, the seasoning was just right when you scooped it up in moderation.

What really surprised me was that after ordering, it came back late because I was doing something else.

There was no ramen on the table....

That's right... it was a system where ramen was not served if the customer was not present (!!!!)

I asked the staff about this and received a confirmation, so it was correct.

I could see how much care was taken about the doneness of the noodles, and with that anticipation in mind, I hurriedly stirred the ramen and served the noodles...

It came out with thin noodles which I didn't like.

But I didn't think much of it. Because I had the mindset that I was just going to eat a little and catch the train and just fill my stomach and go.

But here, my perception of my thin side was completely shattered.

Who would look for al dente in ramen?

Who...not pasta

The moment I chewed the noodles, I was so embarrassed by the chewy texture that felt like it was bouncing off my teeth, but even if I kept chewing, the same texture just repeated itself.

From then on, the previous situations flashed through my mind, and I realized that this was not a coincidence, so I quickly ate the soup.

hmm. also. salty. However, various rich and strong scents gently hit you one after another.

So, I felt that the strengths and advantages of Japanese ramen were well localized to Koreans, with little likes or dislikes.

If you're someone like me who pays even a little bit of attention when eating, the quality is so incredible that you'll never notice it.

Unlike other restaurants that rely on turnover when it comes to ramen,

If you can customize the thickness of the broth and the doneness of the noodles, and the price is the same as other places,

This is Michelin, but where on earth is Michelin?

Also, if you cook chashu too much, it turns into soybean paste, and if you cook it poorly, it turns into boiled pork.

I still don't know which is the true chashu, but I think it's about 7 to 3 between boiled pork and grilled pork.

I think it would be nice if the stores that were able to implement that so precisely and sell really crappy frozen char siu for 4,000 won for three would please reflect.

Again, I heard that real Japanese ramen is so greasy and salty that Koreans can't even scoop more than one spoonful.

If this is the case, the localization has been done to perfection.

I also had regular broth this time, but next time I plan to order thick broth and firm noodles.

I had even planned a trip to Japan to see what true Japanese ramen was, but something came up so I canceled it.

I felt so good because I felt like I had traveled to Japan for only 16,000 won.

ah. And when I went in and sat down, there were no customers, but by the time I left, there were full tables.

Don't believe useless reviews. Don't even trust my review.

To be sure, you just have to look at whether the store is a place where you can eat in line or have a pool table.

reviews.author: Riu Noh
reviews.text:
[This is my first negative review]

The food was okay, but the service was worst. (Especially the female employee wearing glasses) Two people went and ordered over 60,000 won.

The menu information said 'ball rice service', so I ordered one first, and the size of rice served was the size provided in the soy sauce sauce.

Seeing the amount I received, my companion ordered two, but he refused, saying it was only one bowl of rice per person. We politely asked if we could order it for three people, but were refused. So, even though I expressed my intention to “pay additionally,” I received a response that additional orders were not possible.

The important thing is that there was no limit to one item per person anywhere in the store, and this process was very unfriendly.

In that case, it would be a good idea to create a menu so that you can order for an additional fee. It feels pitiful to waste such an enjoyable dining experience just for barely a bowl of rice.

From a customer's perspective, I don't want to come back again due to the incomprehensible rules and unfriendly customer service. The taste of basic tonkotsu ramen is decent, but please take into account that the standard of ramen restaurants in Seoul is rising.

I went to Abiko for lunch today. Abiko is the place that comes to mind whenever I have curry cravings, so I tend to go there often, but on this day, I was particularly craving curry, so I ordered the whole sirloin pork cutlet curry, curry udon, and vegetable & pork curry. Ordering was easy through the kiosk, and as always, the atmosphere of the store was clean and clutter-free, making it great for dining.

The first menu item that came out was the pork loin pork cutlet curry, and the tonkatsu that day was exceptionally delicious. The batter is not thick and the meat is not dry, so every time you chew it, it feels slightly crunchy and the inside feels moist? Abiko curry basically has a strong flavor and consistency, and it goes perfectly well with the tonkatsu, which balances out the heaviness well. The curry was not too salty and still had a nutty flavor, so it was good to eat neatly. I chose level 2, and the spiciness was mild enough that even people who can't eat spicy food could eat it comfortably.

The curry udon that I ordered together had a richer and thicker broth than I expected, so as soon as I took a bite, I thought, “Oh, that’s right, Abiko is a slightly steamed udon.” The udon noodles are well-boiled and firm, so it feels like they're coated in the curry broth. It was a moment when the chopsticks became busier than the spoon. Even though it was level 2 spiciness, the soup was savory and not overpowering, and it was even more memorable in cold weather.

And lastly, vegetable & pork curry. Personally, it was the menu I was most satisfied with that day. The vegetables were cut into large pieces, so they had a good chew, and there was just the right amount of meat, so it was well-balanced. In particular, Abiko's unique sweet, savory, and salty flavors felt harmonious and went well with the rice. The vegetables weren't too soft and were alive enough, so the texture was good. There was no greasiness at all, so I ate it without any worries until the end.

The total price was 24,100 won, and considering the cost of eating out these days, I think Abiko is still an acceptable price for the quality. It's rare to find a place where the portions are just right and the depth of the curry taste remains the same, so if you like curry, it's definitely worth a visit at least once. Anyone can enjoy it as long as they adjust the spiciness level carefully when selecting the menu.

Overall, I was satisfied with my visit that day, and I 100% intend to visit again. The tonkatsu is in good condition and I plan to go again when I crave soup and curry. In particular, curry udon is more addictive than you think, so I highly recommend it to udon lovers!

reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
The moment I saw the owner at the kitchen counter, I was shocked because he resembled YouTuber ‘God of Business’ Eun Hyun-jang.
Fortunately, the only thing they resemble is their appearance, and the service is more friendly than expected.
However, the halls are large compared to the manpower, so the service flow is hectic and the time between courses is long.

If the reservation is successful, I am willing to come again.
It is not a course that will tear your stomach, but rather a ‘moderately full’ course.
If I only think about the shortcomings, the additional 2,000 won for the palace is a bit of a waste, and the quality of the wine glass is not satisfactory, but overall, it is still a good thing.

Start with mozuku, red shrimp, and sesame sauce.
It opens the mouth in a refreshing way, but the sesame flavor is disappointingly weaker than expected.
Immediately, the raw mackerel touches down.
It was light and firm without any fishy taste, and the quantity was generous, but it would have been more fun to chew if the cut had been just one size larger.

The braised monkfish liver was a bit fishy to my friend, but by my standards, it was prepared neatly and the flavor came first.
Sashimi, amberjack, and tuna sashimi all have different textures.
The tuna has a light, ‘honest white meat’, the amberjack is slightly chewy but has a good chew thanks to its chewiness, and the tuna has a distinct iron flavor that seems to be divided into likes and dislikes—I got what my companion left behind.

Negitoro is finished with a ‘rich version’, with a little bit of uni and a generous sprinkle of ikura.
They say Donghan is the top of the day, but I was disappointed with the quality of the seaweed.
If I had known this would happen, I would have given Kim up to my companion who liked Kim.

The abalone intestine pasta was an unexpected hit.
The thick intestine sauce without any fishiness coats the noodles well.
However, because the noodles have a ‘meal-style dry noodle’ feel, they lack the elasticity to support the flavor and consistency.

The mackerel sushi was as light as a can of tuna with a slightly burnt flavor, and the sea bream sashimi (lightly grilled) that followed was attractive with its lightness and very faint sea scent.
The horse mackerel marinated in soybean paste had the unique crunchy texture of the horse mackerel, but the combination of soybean paste, which resembles chewy brown rice grains, may be ambiguous depending on your taste.
The fried eel is chewy, like sweet and sour pork, but the presence of the flesh is weak, so the texture is closer to ‘fried skin’.

The chicken wing dumplings almost completely removed the fishy flavor characteristic of chicken skin, so even though I'm not good at eating chicken skin, I enjoyed a few bites of it - but I wish the dumpling filling was a little more delicious.
The Geumtae pot rice had so little Geumtae in it that people asked, “Does it have Geumtae in it?” It's a position I want to be in, but the fact that I saw Geumtae in this price range feels like a favor in itself.
The finale is Gyoku.
The surface is square with a thin glaze of sugar, and the inside is fluffy like castella—“It’s not like they keep insisting that egg rolls are called gyoku these days,” but it turned out to be the real thing.

In general, there are clear advantages in the spectrum of white and green meat that is pulled out neatly, the internal sauces, and the gyoku.
On the other hand, there is room for improvement in hardware such as glasses, refills, and additional toppings, noodle quality, and slight differences in some combinations.
Still, it is a house that is cost-effective and fun enough to make you say “I’ll go again” once you make a reservation.

Among the Vietnamese foods I've tried in Korea, this is the closest restaurant to the local taste.
I don't know if the kitchen chef is Vietnamese, but except for the ingredients, it feels like eating in Vietnam.
I had spicy seafood rice noodles and gum seung (Vietnamese pork ribs and rice), and they tasted amazing.
Rice noodles have a unique flavor as the unique taste of spices goes well with the spiciness.
Gum Seung's pork ribs taste a little weaker than the Vietnamese ones in terms of seasoning, flavor, and thickness, but it's still edible.
Other beef rice noodles and fried noodles are also worth enjoying.

reviews.author: Gourmet Tourist (danzzanaz)
reviews.text:
📌Assorted rice noodles
Assorted rice noodles are rice noodles with brisket and beef brisket.
Since there are two types of meat, there is a lot of meat involved.
The soup is a clear soup made in the style of Vietnamese rice noodles.
I think it feels clearer rather than thicker.
It contains a lot of noodles and meat, so it’s a filling meal.

As it is a traditional Vietnamese dish, bean sprouts are not included, but lemon cilantro is provided upon request.
You can eat it with toppings according to your taste.

📌Buncha
Buncha comes with noodles, vegetables and meat.
It is eaten by dipping it in sauce. The sauce is a light diluted chili sauce.
I liked that the vegetables were really fresh.
The meat was also good to eat.

Personally, I liked buncha better than rice noodles.

📌Half and half roll
This menu comes with half shrimp roll and crab roll.
The shrimp roll was more delicious.
The fried rice paper was really crispy and delicious.

When you order one menu per person, rice noodles are refilled so you can have a hearty meal.

I felt the owner was friendly, so I had no complaints about the service.

However, it doesn't feel very special, and it's just a good place to go if you're nearby rather than a place you come from far away to eat.

translation

📌Assorted Rice Noodles
Assorted Rice Noodles is a rice noodle dish that includes lamb and beef. Since two types of meat are used, it has a lot of meat. The soup is clear like Vietnamese rice noodles, rather than cloudy like Korean-style soup. It has a clearer taste than a steamed one. It is hearty to eat since it has a lot of noodles and meat.

Since it is a traditional Vietnamese dish, it does not contain bean sprouts. However, if you request it, they will bring you lemon and basil. It is good to eat with toppings according to your preference.

📌Bun Cha
Bun Cha is a dish that consists of noodles, vegetables, and meat. It is eaten by dipping it in the sauce. The sauce is a lightly diluted chili sauce. The vegetables are very fresh, and the meat is also good to eat.

Personally, I found Bun Cha to be more to my liking than the rice noodles.

📌 Banh Mi Roll
This is a menu where shrimp rolls and crab rolls are served in equal amounts. The shrimp roll was tasty. It is a menu where rice paper is fried, making it really crispy and delicious.

If you order one menu per person, the rice noodles will be refilled, so you can have a hearty meal.

I felt that the owner was kind, so I had no complaints about the service.

However, it's not a place that gives you an extremely special feeling, but rather a good place to go if you're just in the area
